body:
Three open issues from real reporters were found today to have been fully fixed and
released weeks earlier, with the reporter never told:

* #876 (@KucharczykL, CWA_DB.execute_write) — fixed in v4.1.13 (0f03c2784, #901).
  We wrote "I'll post back here once it's in a release." 26 days, no post.
* #877 (@yodatak, PDF reload) — fixed in the SAME release, v4.1.13 (986ac8f77, #904),
  both the parse fix and the new-UI button the reporter also asked for. 26 days, no post.
* #579 (@uschi1, light design + read mark) — both halves delivered; the reporter had
  even CONFIRMED the light theme themselves in #351 on 2026-07-27. We wrote "will follow
  up here once it lands" on 07-11 and never did.

The shape: the `promised` label captures the commitment at the moment it is made, which
works. Nothing ever sweeps that label back against shipped releases, so the promise is
tracked but never discharged. Two of the three trace to one release (v4.1.13), which
suggests the failure is per-release-sweep, not per-issue.

Why it matters: these are the highest-trust threads we have — a user who reported a real
bug, got a specific diagnosis, and was promised a follow-up. The fix existing and the user
knowing about it are different things, and only the second one ends their problem. It also
inflates the promise backlog with items that are actually done, which buries the ones that
are not.

Suggested mechanism (not implemented here): extend the awaiting-verification sweep in
scripts/auto-close-awaiting-verification.sh, or the followup-board generator, to also list
open `promised` issues whose referenced fix appears in a published release — the same
cross-reference against CHANGES-vs-upstream.md / CHANGELOG.md that post-release-outreach.sh
already does for upstream threads. The board currently reports owe_reply=0 for these
because our comment was last, which is exactly why they were invisible.
title: Fixes ship but the originating issue never gets its close-out, so reporters sit on solved problems
